units.text: INT. PERFUMERY - PARIS - AFTERNOON
A shop of glass and brass.
Rows of tiny bottles glow in the amber light.
Orange blossom and jasmine hang thick in the air.
ARMAND LAFORGUE, 50s, the master perfumer, stirs a vial at the counter.
He does not look up.
The bell above the door chimes, and ISIDORE BEAUCAIRE, 40s, a courtier in a powdered wig, steps in, shaking rain from his coat.
Armand. You look well.
units.name: ISIDORE

units.text: I am not well, Isidore. I am merely alive.
units.name: ARMAND

units.text: He sets down the vial.
He pours a measure into a crystal stopper and offers it.
The courtier sniffs, smiles, and hands it back.
Violet and cedar.
units.name: ISIDORE

units.text: And?
units.name: ARMAND

units.text: And something I cannot name.
units.name: ISIDORE

units.text: Bitter almond.
units.name: ARMAND

units.text: Isidore's smile dies.
He steps back.
His hand drifts to his coat.
Armand watches it go, then lifts the stopper to his own lips and drinks it down.
You see? Harmless.
units.name: ARMAND

units.text: The courtier stares.
Armand sets the empty stopper on the counter and places both hands flat on the wood.
The other bottle, however, is in your pocket.
units.name: ARMAND

units.text: He lunges across the counter and seizes the wrist.
They struggle among the vials.
Glass breaks.
The scent of a hundred flowers erupts at once.
Isidore breaks free and runs for the door.
He yanks it open.
Armand sags against the shelves, laughing quietly.
